source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Transference, in which the client redirects feelings or expectations from past relationships toward the current nurse.","B":"Countertransference, in which the clinician's own past experiences shape emotional reactions toward the current client.","C":"Regression, in which a person reverts to an earlier developmental pattern of coping when under significant stress.","D":"Sublimation, in which an unacceptable impulse is redirected into a socially acceptable activity or constructive outlet."}}
source_row.rationale: Transference is the redirection of feelings or expectations from an important past relationship onto the current clinician; it is not by itself evidence of a personality disorder.
source_row.source_detail: Therapeutic relationship section defines transference as a client's transfer of feelings associated with significant people in the past onto the nurse or other current caregiver. source_row.stem: A client responds to the nurse as though the nurse were a significant person from the client's past. What is this phenomenon?
